commentary.text: I’m claiming a central square immediately, establishing Red’s presence in the victory zone while keeping clear lines for Yellow to reinforce later.

I’m taking a central foothold on (4,4) while avoiding the immediate Red sandwich available against (3,4). The plan is to contest the remaining center squares with Green and force Team A to spend moves breaking our formation.
Yellow takes the second central square, building a connected Red–Yellow foothold and forcing Team B to respond to our center control.
I’m developing Green to (2,3), directly pressuring Red’s central blocker. If Red vacates (3,3), Green can claim it; if Yellow later clears (4,3), Green may build a vertical sandwich against Red.
Red occupies the third central square. Blue now has to vacate or defend its lone center point, while Yellow is poised to fill any opening on the next move.

I’m exploiting the vertical alignment created by Red’s last move: Blue lands on (2,4), using the Blue piece at (4,4) as the far flank to sandwich and capture Red on (3,4). This preserves our center foothold while reducing Red toward elimination.
Yellow attacks horizontally instead: landing at (4,5) uses the Yellow piece at (4,3) as the far flank, sandwiching and capturing Blue’s central piece.
I’m clearing (2,3) while keeping Green centralized at (2,2). If Red vacates (3,3), the Green piece on (3,0) can claim that center square; otherwise Blue remains poised to occupy (4,4).
Red develops beside the center at (3,5), creating a two-step center completion: Yellow can occupy (4,4), after which this Red piece can slide into (3,4).

I’m re-establishing Blue on (4,4), the safest central foothold available. Yellow’s pieces on either side cannot capture it without first vacating and later returning, giving us time to react while keeping Team A from consolidating the center.

Yellow steps temporarily to (5,5), preserving the horizontal capture mechanism. After Red fills (3,4), Blue must either vacate (4,4), allowing another Yellow to occupy it, or remain and be sandwiched when this piece returns to (4,5).

I’m shifting Green to (2,4) to prepare a direct entry into the open center square (3,4). This also supports future coordination around Blue’s foothold at (4,4) without exposing Green to an immediate sandwich.
Red now fills (3,4), completing the upper half of the center and activating Yellow’s fork against Blue’s piece at (4,4).

I’m developing Blue to (6,3), a safe staging square that avoids creating another immediate sandwich target. Yellow can attack our center foothold next, so this move preserves Blue’s mobility while positioning a reserve near the lower center for the ensuing fight.
Yellow returns to (4,5), triggering the prepared sandwich against Blue at (4,4). Removing that blocker opens the final central square for Yellow to occupy on its next turn.

I’m placing Green on (4,2) as a close flank against Yellow’s central anchor. If (4,4) becomes reachable, Green can land there and sandwich the Yellow piece on (4,3), breaking Team A’s center formation.
Red moves to (3,6), closing Blue’s horizontal route along row 3 while leaving our three occupied central squares untouched. Yellow remains ready to step from (4,5) into the open final center square.

I’m moving Blue to (6,4) to obstruct Yellow’s vertical route toward the center while keeping a reserve aligned beneath the central fight. Yellow’s piece on (4,5) remains the critical immediate threat.
Yellow steps into (4,4), completing Team A’s occupation of all four central squares for the immediate center victory.
